segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Silence filled the cavernous chamber. Only the slow, backwards ticking of the Great Clock echoed through the dark:

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: You pick up Pip’s crooked tweed hat, clutching it against your chest as tears stream down your cheeks.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Heavy wooden boots stomped onto the catwalk. Two nine-foot Clockwork Praetorians seized you by the arms, twisting your hands behind your back and forcing you to your knees.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The Clockmaker bent down, picked up Barnaby's forged silver cog with his brass-tipped fingers, and examined it with a cruel, mocking smile.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: A pity it will never turn.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The Clockmaker walked slowly toward you, standing over you on the catwalk. He looked down with cold, venomous triumph.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: the Clockmaker sneered, his voice booming through the cathedral of gears.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Captured. Defeated. Alone. Your little fox is erased from existence. Your master-smith is locked in an iron cage. You have NO ONE left to help you!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He leaned in close, his silver hair glinting in the dark.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: You will never touch the Great Clock. You will never stop the reverse countdown. And you will never see your friends or your world ever again.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He raised his obsidian pocket-watch, preparing to lock you in chains forever.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And that's when you hear it.
